## Panama in One Trip

Panama City brings together two eras. In Panamá Viejo, you can see the ruins of cathedrals dating to the early 17th century, along with the remains of monasteries and bridges. In the newer part of the city, modern neighbourhoods sit alongside Casco Antiguo, a colonial district of narrow streets, squares and historic buildings.

From the city, the route takes you into the tropics. In Chagres, you will learn about Emberá life and crafts, travel along the river in a traditional dugout canoe and have the chance to swim by a waterfall. Spend a day by the Pacific Ocean on Taboga, then take a motorboat trip in Soberanía and on Gatún Lake to islands where you may see monkeys, crocodiles, turtles and, with luck, manatees.

On the Caribbean leg, you will visit Fort San Lorenzo and the Panama Canal. The final major excursion takes you to El Valle de Antón, a volcanic caldera with a market, Chorro El Macho waterfall, tropical forest and a botanical garden.
